record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Determine whether the following statements hold: (1) for every computably enumerable set A, there is a computably enumerable set D ⊆ 2^N such that A ≡_rK D and both conditional plain complexities C(A↾n | D↾n) and C(D↾n | A↾n) are O(1); and (2) for every real x, there is a random real z such that z ≥_rK x, or at least z ≥_K x.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Are the following true? (1) For any c.e. set A, there exists a c.e. set D ⊆ 2N, such that A ≡rK D and C(A ↾ n|D ↾ n) = C(D ↾ n|A ↾ n) = O(1); (2) For all x, there is a random z such that z ≥rK x (or z ≥K x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. For a finite binary string σ, let C(σ) denote its plain Kolmogorov complexity, i.e. the length of a shortest program (with respect to a fixed optimal universal Turing machine without prefix-freeness restriction) that outputs σ. Let K(σ) denote the prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity. For a (possibly infinite) binary sequence X ∈ 2^N, write X ↾ n for its initial segment of length n, and define C(σ | τ) and K(σ | τ) as the corresponding conditional complexities.

For X, Y ∈ 2^N, define the relative Kolmogorov reducibilities:
 • X ≤_K Y iff there is a constant c such that K(X ↾ n | Y ↾ n) ≤ c for all n.
 • X ≤_rK Y (relative-K reducibility) iff there is a constant c such that K(X ↾ n) ≤ K(Y ↾ n) + c for all n (equivalently, the prefix complexities of initial segments of X are bounded by those of Y up to an additive constant).
Write X ≡_rK Y when X ≤_rK Y and Y ≤_rK X.

A set A ⊆ N is identified with its characteristic sequence in 2^N. Call A computably enumerable (c.e.) if it is the range of a computable function (equivalently, Σ⁰₁). A real z ∈ 2^N is called (Martin-Löf) random if there is no c.e. sequence of open sets U_n ⊆ 2^N with measure(U_n) ≤ 2^{−n} such that z ∈ ⋂_n U_n.

Question. Decide whether each of the following statements is true:

(1) For every computably enumerable set A ⊆ N, there exists a computably enumerable set D (viewed as an element of 2^N) such that A ≡_rK D and, for some constant c independent of n,
  C(A ↾ n | D ↾ n) ≤ c  and  C(D ↾ n | A ↾ n) ≤ c  for all n ∈ N.

(2) For every real x ∈ 2^N there exists a Martin-Löf random real z ∈ 2^N such that z ≥_rK x; or, in the weaker form, z ≥_K x.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of either part (the c.e. ≡_rK companion problem, or the existence of a random real above an arbitrary real in ≥_rK or ≥_K). The status appears to remain open.
